runtime.help_excerpt:
Run a selected profiler

Usage:
  dircue analyze [flags]
  dircue analyze [command]

Available Commands:
  all          Combine language statistics, ecosystem hints, and selected profilers
  availability Inspect source-acquisition boundaries without fetching content
  declarations Read static project declarations and named interfaces
  discovery    Inventory file metadata and candidate manifests or artifacts
  ecosystems   Report ecosystems inferred from supported filename and manifest hints
  environments Map declared project environments without running builds
  explain      Explain one file decision or retained project relationship
  focus        Profile a declared project with its original-root context
  formats      Inspect bounded content for format evidence
  frameworks   Report frameworks inferred from supported filename and manifest hints
  graph        Describe static .NET project-reference graphs
  languages    Classify source languages with Linguist-compatible statistics
  metrics      Count lines, comments, code, and lexical complexity with scc
  packages     Import an existing Syft JSON report with project context
  projects     Discover supported project manifests and shared build inputs
  registries   Observe selected NuGet and npm package-source declarations
  rules        Apply explicit rules to selected file metadata and bounded content
  structure    Measure supported syntax through an explicitly supplied native worker

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for analyze

Global Flags:
  -b, --breakdown            Include file paths in language results
  -j, --json                 Emit JSON
      --max-file-bytes int   Skip files larger than this many bytes (0 disables the optional size limit)
      --on-error string      Per-file read errors: fail or continue with explicit omissions (default "fail")
  -r, --rev string           Git revision to analyze (default "HEAD")
      --source string        Content source: auto (Git when present), git, or directory (default "auto")
  -s, --strategies           Show the language detection strategy for each file (text output)
      --tree string          Exact Git tree object ID to analyze (mutually exclusive with --rev)
  -t, --tree-size int        Maximum number of files scanned (default 100000)
      --workers int          Number of concurrent file workers (0 selects automatically)

Use "dircue analyze [command] --help" for more information about a command.

runtime.help_excerpt:
Run the default language and filename-based detectors in one scan. Optional profilers run only when requested through flags such as --discovery, --declarations, --environments, --metrics, and --structure. Each module retains its own population, coverage, and omissions; totals need not describe identical files. Structural analysis requires an explicitly selected worker.

Usage:
  dircue analyze all [path] [flags]

Examples:
  dircue analyze all --discovery --json /content
  dircue analyze all --declarations --environments --metrics --json /checkout

Flags:
      --availability                    Inspect bounded source-availability evidence without fetching missing material
      --declarations                    Read declared project identities, workspace relationships, requirements, and interfaces
      --discovery                       Summarize regular-file metadata and candidate manifests/artifacts
      --environments                    Map declared project environments using manifest evidence and bounded global.json inputs
      --files                           Include per-file metrics or structural observations
      --formats                         Inspect bounded content for format evidence, including data and artifact files
      --functions                       Include bounded function-space metrics from the structural worker
      --graph                           Analyze static .NET project-reference graphs (includes project inventory)
  -h, --help                            help for all
      --hotspots                        Summarize measured function populations and retain highest-valued metric evidence
      --metrics                         Count code, comment, and blank lines and estimate complexity with scc
      --metrics-max-file-bytes int      Skip metrics for larger files; maximum 268435456 bytes (default 16777216)
      --metrics-scope string            Metrics selection: source (language statistics) or text (all detected text languages) (default "source")
      --projects                        Map projects, declared build requirements, and content composition
      --registries                      Read selected NuGet.Config and .npmrc declarations; disclose qualified names and sanitized origins
      --rules-file string               Apply an explicit caller-supplied JSON ruleset; never discovers rulesets automatically
      --structural-max-file-bytes int   Maximum complete source bytes for structural analysis (at most 8388608) (default 8388608)
      --structural-timeout duration     Time limit for each structural worker invocation (default 10s)
      --structural-worker string        Path to the optional native structural worker
      --structure                       Run optional structural analysis with the specified worker
      --syft-report string              Import a previously generated Syft JSON report; does not execute Syft
      --syft-report-max-bytes int       Maximum imported report bytes (at most 134217728) (default 16777216)
      --syft-report-sha256 string       Report digest for a caller-supplied source binding; requires --syft-source-tree
      --syft-root string                Explicit report coordinate root mapped to this inventory (commonly /)
      --syft-source-tree string         Git tree the caller attests was cataloged; requires --syft-report-sha256

runtime.help_excerpt:
Run a trusted structural worker on bounded selected source files. Requires --structural-worker; the worker is executable code, not a sandbox. Unsupported languages, parse errors, file limits, and module scope remain visible. --functions adds function records; --hotspots ranks supported measurements without assigning a software-quality grade.

Usage:
  dircue analyze structure [path] [flags]

Examples:
  dircue analyze structure --structural-worker /tools/dircue-structural-worker --json /checkout
  dircue analyze structure --structural-worker /tools/dircue-structural-worker --functions --hotspots --json /checkout

Flags:
      --files                           Include per-file metrics or structural observations
      --functions                       Include bounded function-space metrics from the structural worker
  -h, --help                            help for structure
      --hotspots                        Summarize measured function populations and retain highest-valued metric evidence
      --structural-max-file-bytes int   Maximum complete source bytes for structural analysis (at most 8388608) (default 8388608)
      --structural-timeout duration     Time limit for each structural worker invocation (default 10s)
      --structural-worker string        Path to the optional native structural worker

Global Flags:
  -b, --breakdown            Include file paths in language results
  -j, --json                 Emit JSON
      --max-file-bytes int   Skip files larger than this many bytes (0 disables the optional size limit)
      --on-error string      Per-file read errors: fail or continue with explicit omissions (default "fail")

      --source string        Content source: auto (Git when present), git, or directory (default "auto")
  -s, --strategies           Show the language detection strategy for each file (text output)
      --tree string          Exact Git tree object ID to analyze (mutually exclusive with --rev)
  -t, --tree-size int        Maximum number of files scanned (default 100000)
      --workers int          Number of concurrent file workers (0 selects automatically)
